clue.text: Constellation a spy associated with a memorandum we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken phrase, so the clue's words are taken by their sound rather than their spelling

parts.words: a spy associated with a memorandum
parts.note: Quiller is the secret agent of the spy novel and film The Quiller Memorandum, so 'a spy' of that memorandum is 'a Quiller'

explanation.surface: An agent linked to a secret memo turns out to be a star group, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud with a non-rhotic accent, 'a Quiller' matches the eagle constellation's Latin name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquila, the Eagle, is a named group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Organ stops and soprano accompanies Peter in Britten opera

parts.note: Peter Quint is the ghostly valet in Britten's opera The Turn of the Screw
S is the standard abbreviation for soprano in vocal scores

explanation.surface: A singer joins a character on stage in a Britten production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanies' simply links the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A quint is an organ register sounding a fifth above the written pitch, so several are stops of that kind.

clue.text: Decorate top of cake — that's about it!

indicators.note: 'about' says the abbreviation for 'that's' is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means 'that is'

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A baker puts the finishing touch on a cake and declares the job done.
explanation.walkthrough: IE goes round C, the first letter of 'cake'; 'it' is left as a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice a cake is to adorn it with a sugary coating.

clue.text: Name of quartet, one at origin of music-making here in France

parts.note: the article 'a' means one

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: ici is French for 'here'

explanation.surface: A string quartet's name traced to where music-making began in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' links the pieces; the Amici Quartet is a British string quartet whose name is Italian for 'friends'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amici is a well-known chamber ensemble, so its title names a quartet.

clue.text: & 26A: Work of 11 showing how a lawn is cleared of moss?

definitions.meaning: an opera by the composer at 11 across, the man behind The Firebird

definitions.text: showing how a lawn is cleared of moss?
definitions.meaning: a garden tool being dragged across the grass, step by step, making headway

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the title literally: a garden implement's advance across the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's 1951 opera, after Hogarth's prints, follows Tom Rakewell's decline.

clue.text: Goethe, say, in Italy, incompetently escorted? That's not right!

indicators.note: done incompetently, so the letters of the word escorted are botched into a new order
'That's not' tells us one letter is missing from the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: A German visitor in Italy is badly shown around, and complains it is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from ESCORTED to leave ESCOTED, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedesco is Italian for a German man, and Goethe was a famous German who travelled in Italy.

clue.text: Was Montaigne first one of such to support French art say?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Was Montaigne first one of such to support French art say?' (9): ES (French art) + SAY gives ESSAY, but no parse found for the remaining ISTS that uses the other words without strain.
annotationWithheld.clue: Was Montaigne first one of such to support French art say?

clue.text: An Egyptian goddess stifling desperate groan in dramatic denouement

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Isis is the Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters of groan are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity muffles an anguished moan at a play's climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifling' has the goddess phrase close round the jumbled moan; the term comes from Aristotle's Poetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Anagnorisis is Aristotle's term for the moment of recognition when a tragic hero discovers the truth.

clue.text: Fashion Fleming incorporated in directions for schoolboys

indicators.note: incorporated in means placed within, so the two pieces sit inside the compass points

parts.note: E and S are compass directions, east and south
ton is an old word for fashion or high style
Ian Fleming, creator of James Bond

explanation.surface: Bond's author is credited with directing a fashion for boys.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleming himself went to Eton, a famous English boarding school, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Etonians are pupils of Eton College, a boys' school.

clue.text: Ballet to see performed at La Fenice?

definitions.text: Ballet to see performed at La Fenice?

parts.words: Ballet to see performed at La Fenice?
parts.note: La Fenice, the Venice opera house, means 'The Phoenix', a flaming bird, so a fitting ballet there is Stravinsky's one about a magical blazing bird

explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's 1910 ballet about a magical glowing bird suits a theatre named after the phoenix.

clue.text: Does a Glaucus, to start with, perhaps qualify as one?

definitions.text: Does a Glaucus, to start with, perhaps qualify as one?

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be arranged otherwise
to start with picks out the opening letter

explanation.surface: A question whether a mythical figure counts as one of a divine class.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange DOESA plus G, Glaucus's first letter; Glaucus was a fisherman who became a marine deity, making the clue whole a definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaucus in Greek myth was a fisherman turned immortal of the ocean.

clue.text: Composer who's blue about almost starving badly

indicators.note: badly suggests a mess, so the remaining letters are rearranged
almost means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: the sky is blue, a stock crossword equivalence

explanation.surface: A composer is depressed about nearly starving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's' and 'about' are link words here, so the jumble simply comes before the colour; 'almost' trims the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian-born creator of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Coiffing's not hard as touching up pictures

indicators.note: not says a letter is left out of the hairdressing word

parts.note: coiffing is dressing hair, here with a brush
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Doing someone's hair gently is like retouching photos.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop H from HAIRBRUSHING; 'as' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Airbrushing is spraying paint to retouch photographs, removing blemishes.

clue.text: Diamond concealed by someone illegally?

indicators.note: concealed by says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gem smuggled away by a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' looks like a gem but is the singer Neil Diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is the first name of singer-songwriter Diamond.

clue.text: Ballet in which you'llsee priest going wild about having a band

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the next piece
going wild signals a jumble of the letters of priest

parts.note: 'of' can mean having, as in 'a man of means'
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A ballet in which a cleric runs riot with a group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wild' jumbles the cleric to RITESP, which 'about' wraps around the piece from 'having'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring is a 1913 ballet score.

clue.text: Milne character's not good, I heard — stone me!

indicators.note: not means one letter is removed from the bouncing tiger's name

parts.note: Tigger is the tiger in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh

indicators.note: heard tells us the pronoun is taken by its sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at hearing about a children's book character.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one G from TIGGER'S; I said aloud gives EYE. 'Stone me!' is a British exclamation of surprise, and 'me' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger's eye is a golden-brown banded quartz used as a gem.

clue.text: Partner for Gala to love endlessly after most of Valse Excentrique

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
excentrique is French for eccentric, so the letters are rearranged
most of means the last letter is lost
endlessly removes the final letter

parts.note: to love is to adore

explanation.surface: A dance partner adores a quirky waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: Valse Excentrique is itself a Stravinsky piece, so 'Excentrique' doubles neatly as the jumble signal; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was married to Gala, his muse.

clue.text: Can you find their songs in catalogue surrounded by confused diagrams?

indicators.note: surrounded by means one piece sits within the other
confused signals the letters of diagrams are mixed up

parts.note: a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A puzzle about tracking down songs in an index within muddled charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles the charts, which then go round the catalogue word; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrigalists write or sing part-songs of the Renaissance, so the songs belong to them.

clue.text: Pulses, say, in the cavities of blood vessels without number

indicators.note: in places one piece within another
without means losing a letter

parts.note: lumens are the inner channels of tubes like arteries
e.g. means 'for example', which is 'say'

explanation.surface: Throbbing in veins described medically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulses' looks like heartbeats but is beans and lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes are plants with seed pods, lentils and peas among them.

clue.text: Composition that takes only a short time when ending's transposed

indicators.note: the last two letters swap places

parts.note: a minute is a short time

explanation.surface: A piece of music lasting only moments.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuet is a stately dance in triple time, and music for it.

clue.text: Composer of pensive songs?

indicators.note: 'of' signals letters taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Who wrote these wistful songs?
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Ives was an American modernist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer.

clue.text: Ruler's standing in London Park with joint

parts.note: Regent's Park is a royal park in London
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A monarch's position in a London park with a sore joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A regentship is the office held by one who governs for a monarch.

clue.text: Type one's associated with operatic priestess

parts.note: a norm is a standard type
A is one

explanation.surface: A model of a kind associated with opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's Druid priestess heroine.

clue.text: Recommend what needs consent, according to Drury

definitions.meaning: to counsel or suggest a course

definitions.text: what needs consent, according to Drury
definitions.meaning: Allen Drury's novel ... and Consent pairs the word with consent

explanation.definitionFit: To recommend is to counsel someone.

clue.text: Greek God featuring in the opening of Mavra and a composition of 11

indicators.note: the opening is the first letter

parts.note: Orpheus is a 1947 ballet by Stravinsky

explanation.surface: A Greek deity appears in a Stravinsky opera opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Mavra is a one-act Stravinsky opera; 'and' and 'featuring in' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Morpheus is the Greek god of dreams.

clue.text: Here's evidence of drunkenness

definitions.meaning: the sound of a tipsy hiccup

explanation.definitionFit: Hic is Latin for 'here', and also the written sound of a hiccup.

clue.text: See 5
May Louisa have an alternative arrangement with this novelist?

definitions.text: May Louisa have an alternative arrangement with this novelist?

parts.words: May Louisa have an alternative arrangement with this novelist?
parts.note: the novelist's names swap order: Louisa May, author of Little Women

explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist who wrote Little Women.
